_comment: LOCKED visual + audio identity for the local render pipeline. Every future scene/video MUST reuse these exact values byte-for-byte — do not drift per-video. If a value here ever needs to change, change it once here and re-render, don't override it in a scene spec.

tts._note_google: LOCKED primary engine: unofficial Google Translate TTS (translate.googleapis.com/translate_tts). Free, no key, reachable from this sandbox (confirmed), far more natural than espeak-ng. Text >~180 chars is auto-chunked on sentence/clause boundaries and concatenated (see narrate.py:_split_for_google). If this ever stops being reachable, narrate.py automatically falls back to the espeak-ng settings under fallback_espeak below.
tts._note_piper: piper-tts was installed and would be preferred over both Google TTS and espeak-ng, but its voice models are hosted on huggingface.co, which this sandbox's egress policy blocks (403 on CONNECT, confirmed via /opt/pw-browsers proxy status). See pipeline/README.md 'Blockers' section. If a future environment can reach huggingface.co, swap engine to 'piper' (see narrate.py for the piper code path, left in place but unused).

captions._note_whisper: faster-whisper was installed and IS the preferred captioning method, but its model weights are also fetched from huggingface.co (and the openaipublic.azureedge.net mirror is blocked too, same proxy policy, confirmed 403). Fell back to evenly distributing the KNOWN script words across the measured narration audio duration. This is not true forced-alignment so timing can drift slightly on longer pauses/punctuation, but is deterministic, offline, and close enough for a calm, evenly-paced narrator reading pre-tuned ~20-word lines.
